children: Crude oil contracts rose more than $1/bbl Sunday evening, after U.S. forces attacked two Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz, the first American strike against Tehran in weeks.
At 7:05 p.m. ET, October NYMEX West Texas Intermediate crude prices were up $1.50 to $84.90/bbl. November WTI was $1.35 higher to $83.20/bbl.
London-based November Brent was also up by $1.55 to $89.65/bbl and December Brent was $1.35 higher to $87.45/bbl.
October RBOB was 1.80ct higher to $3.0680/gal and October ULSD was up 5.15cts to $4.3005/gal.

"With strategic petroleum reserves and commercial inventories already at low levels, a further escalation of hostilities could result in prolonged disruption out of the Middle East," said Andy Lipow, President of energy consultant Lipow Oil Associates.

Late Friday, President Trump also confirmed that the U.S. reached a deal with Venezuela to secure control of a big chunk of the Latin American country's oil reserves --estimated at about 300 billion bbl to be the world's largest proven reserves.
